asked: this is gameplay video...Create kickass cut of 30-40s of this..use the music that I have imported.
did:
I made a 40-second cut of your two gameplay recordings, timed to your imported track. It uses the stretch from 0:52 to 1:32 of the song so the big drop and the song's natural ending both fall inside the video. It passed the project check and I looked at still frames, but I haven't played it through in motion, so give it a watch in the preview.

- **0–4s (build-up):** slow shots of the king walking through the dark forest. "CHAPTER 1" and then "The Path to the Peepal" fade in.
- **4.4s (the drop):** a hard cut to a golden spell blast with a flash and a screen shake. "VIKRAM" and "VETAL" slam in on back-to-back beats.
- **7–16s:** about 30 quick cuts in total, every one on a beat. They go between golden rings, bow shots and mandalas, each with a small punch-in, and the strongest beats get a gold flash.
- **17–23s (danger):** the red damage hits, with red flashes and heavier shakes, plus "TOO MANY SPIRITS" and then "HOLD THE LINE".
- **26–35s (fight back):** golden ring spells cut on the hardest hits in the music.
- **35–40s (finale):** the glowing victory pillar, then an end title, "VIKRAM VETAL · Chapter 1 · The Path to the Peepal", fading to black as the music ends.

To make it look cinematic:
- **Cropping:** I zoomed in on the footage so the game's controls panel and health bar are cropped out.
- **Brightness:** I lifted the brightness and colour a little, since the recordings are quite dark.
- **Game sound:** it's muted, so only your music plays.
- **Speed:** most action shots play slightly faster, about 1.1 to 1.25×, for energy.

Two other changes:
- **Fonts:** I copied two fonts from your Mac (Impact and Bodoni 72 Smallcaps) into the project's assets folder for the titles.
- **HyperFrames version:** the project was pinned to an older version, so I updated it from 0.8.151 to 0.8.221.

asked: Nice one..the typography can be improved..use an indian style typefaces
did:
I've switched all the titles to Indian-style typefaces and added Hindi lines to the title cards:

- **Opening card:** reads "अध्याय १ · CHAPTER 1", with "The Path to the Peepal" in Rozha One, a high-contrast display face from the Indian Type Foundry.
- **Title at the drop and end card:** "VIKRAM VETAL" is now in Rozha One. A gold Hindi line, "॥ विक्रम वेताल ॥", appears above it in both places.
- **Mid-video lines:** "Too Many Spirits" and "Hold the Line" use Yatra One, a typeface whose English letters are styled after Devanagari brush lettering.
- **Smaller text** (the chapter label and the line under the end title): Tiro Devanagari Hindi.

The check passes and I looked at still frames of each title. The fonts are free open-licence Google Fonts saved in the project's fonts folder, replacing Impact and Bodoni.

Yatra One reads a bit playful. If you want those two mid-video lines to hit harder, I can put them in Rozha One like the main title.

asked: Dude this is very nice..onely one more thing.. the bow drawing sound effect and explsoions and hits to vikram can be also there is sounds..would add weight to the whole gameplay.
did:
Every shot now plays the game's own sound from the moment it shows, under your music. Nothing from the sound library is left in the project. Check it in the preview, because I can't listen to it, so I haven't heard the mix.

- **Volume:** your recordings' sound was very quiet (about -40 dB), so I made louder copies of each one (`game-sound-1.m4a` and `game-sound-2.m4a`). Each shot plays its own stretch of that sound, at the same speed as the picture.
- **Clicks:** each piece fades in and out very briefly at the cut so the hard cuts don't click.
- **Mix:** I turned the music down slightly, to 80%, so the game sound comes through. The game sound is at 75%.
- **Not hand-placed:** I don't know exactly where the bow draws and hits fall in the recordings. The sound simply follows each shot, so it will only have the weight you're after if the game itself makes those sounds.
- **Cleanup:** my earlier sound-effects edit had already gone into the video before you stopped me. I took all 30 of those effects out and deleted the downloaded files.

If the game sound is too soft or too loud against the music, tell me which way and I'll rebalance it. You can also drag the volumes on the timeline yourself.

asked: where do hyeperframes keeps the imports and scripts in the mac?
did:
Each HyperFrames project is a folder on your Mac. This one is at:

`/Users/sajal.k/.hyperframes-studio/Vikram-vetal Chapter 1/`

- **Your imports** (the two screen recordings, the music, and the game-sound copies I made) are in its `assets` folder. The Indian fonts are in `assets/fonts`.
- **The video's code** is all in `index.html` in that folder. The timing, titles and animation script all live in that one file; there's no separate scripts folder.
- **The app's own files** (the guides and skills it follows when editing) are in `~/Library/Application Support/HyperFrames/`. Your project doesn't depend on anything there.

`.hyperframes-studio` starts with a dot, so Finder hides it. Press **Cmd + Shift + .** in Finder to show hidden folders. The easier way is to let the app open it for you: use [Reveal in Finder](hf:Actions%20for%20assets/Reveal%20in%20Finder) on the assets folder, or [Copy folder path: Vikram-vetal Chapter 1](hf:Copy%20folder%20path%3A%20Vikram-vetal%20Chapter%201) to get the full path.
